newsitem.title: CHINA: Intel sees big China computer market.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees big China computer market.

text.p: China's personal computer buyers are so hungry for new technology that the Chinese market could be the world's second largest after the United States in less than five years, a senior Intel Corp. official said Tuesday.

Intel's new range of Pentium processer chips had pushed aside older lines in 1996 as Chinese personal computer buyers leapfrogged to catch up with technology in the United States, said Intel Vice President Sean Maloney.
Personal computer sales were also rising far faster than in more developed markets elsewhere, Maloney said here.
"I would say that (China) will catch up with Japan as a market in the next three to four years," he said.
"Within the next five years it could be the world's second largest computer market," he said "It's a huge, huge market."
Official estimates put personal computer sales in China at 1.8 million in 1996.
The dramatic expansion of the Chinese market had been a factor in the growing importance to Intel of revenues generated in the Asia-Pacific region, he said.
Asia-Pacific, excluding Japan, had supplied 18 percent of total revenues in 1996, up from 14 percent in 1994, company figures showed.
"I think it will go above 20 percent," Maloney said.

Intel's $99 million flash memory chip assembly and test plant near China's eastern city of Shanghai was expected to be on line before the end of February 1998, said Jim Jarrett, president of Intel China.
The plant, in Shanghai's Pudong free trade zone, is the first phase of a $230 million chip fabrication plan, but no decision had been announced on a second stage, Jarrett said.
